Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Peter Peterson, DOB: Not recorded, Gender: Male, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Dr. Jacob, Practice: Babylon, [Practice Address not recorded]. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD)
- Secondary: Anxiety disorder (possible situational panic attacks)
- Tertiary: Relapsed hypothyroidism (due to cessation of thyroxine; considered due to overlapping symptoms)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Stopped thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented); currently on no medications
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded
- Past Medical History: Hypothyroidism (previously managed with thyroxine; stopped ~3–3.5 months ago)

Mental Health History:

- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): No previous psychological therapies or hospitalizations documented; previously treated for hypothyroidism with thyroxine
- Family History: Not recorded

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Married; some relational difficulty noted (partner complaining of symptoms affecting “nightly activities”); otherwise not specified
- Social Support: Not recorded
- Occupation/Education: Lawyer; recently changed law firms (~3–3.5 months ago)
- Alcohol Use: Not recorded
- Smoking/Substance Use: Not recorded
- Key Stressors: Job change; work stress (“trouble at work”/headaches); marital stress from low energy/affecting intimacy

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not recorded
- Mood & Affect: Reports persistent low mood, feeling “down,” and “out of place”; diminished enjoyment and motivation
- Speech & Thought: Speech coherent; thought content negative (low mood, diminished self-worth implied); cognition intact
- Perception: Denies hallucinations; no abnormal perceptions documented

Cognition:
- Orientation: Not recorded
- Attention/Concentration: Not directly assessed; functional at work, but reports trouble at work and diminished motivation
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Aware of symptoms and seeking help; shows insight into need for clinical assessment

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Not recorded
- Appetite: Decreased appetite for several months
- Motivation/Energy: Markedly reduced energy, difficulty engaging in regular activities (e.g., walking), lack of “umph”
- Anxiety Symptoms: Palpitations and shortness of breath situationally (in lifts), consistent with possible panic episodes; intermittent nausea and headache

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Not recorded
- Protective Factors: Married, employed, demonstrates help-seeking behavior
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Not recorded
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
- Predisposing: Previous history of hypothyroidism; recent major life transition (job change)
- Precipitating: Change of employment; cessation of thyroxine; onset of low mood, fatigue, and decreased appetite shortly after these events
- Perpetuating: Continued low energy and mood, lack of physical activity, functional impact on work and relationship
- Protective: Supportive marital relationship (despite strain); occupational functioning; willingness to seek help

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Understand cause of low mood, low energy, appetite loss, and weight changes; regain prior level of functioning and improve relationship/quality of life
- Clinical Goal(s): Establish diagnosis (major depressive disorder vs. medical/thyroid etiology); restore mood and energy; rule out medical causes (including relapse of hypothyroidism)
- Actions (Patient): Attend recommended blood tests; monitor mood, weight, appetite, and new symptoms; contact GP if symptoms worsen or new physical/mental health concerns arise
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange/refer for blood tests (full panel including anemia, renal/liver/thyroid studies, vitamins); provide psychoeducation; safety net re: urgent symptoms (chest pain, vomiting, bowel changes); review results and refer for further mental health assessment/intervention if indicated

Secondary Problem (Anxiety/Panic Symptoms):
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce/eliminate situational palpitations/shortness of breath (especially in lifts); manage stress more effectively
- Clinical Goal(s): Screen for panic/anxiety disorder; provide basic coping strategies; consider referral for psychological support if persistent/impairing
- Actions (Patient): Track episodes (timing, triggers); practice relaxation or coping techniques if discussed or provided later
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Consider anxiety screening; monitor for persistent, impairing anxiety; provide information/support as needed

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Natural course of depression and fatigue; importance of medical evaluation for possible hypothyroidism/other causes; when to seek urgent/emergency care (e.g., chest pain, sudden vomiting, bowel changes)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Worsening low mood, further weight loss, inability to function at work/home, appearance of suicidal ideation or severe anxiety symptoms, new/worsening physical symptoms
- Coping Strategies: Not formally discussed; recommendation to monitor symptoms and seek help; relaxation/grounding techniques implied for anxiety/panic (not detailed)

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Major Depressive Disorder: High likelihood. Meets criteria for persistent low mood, anergia, appetite/weight loss, and functional impact. Supported by life stressors and current symptom pattern.
- Anxiety Disorder (panic attacks): Medium likelihood. Situational palpitations and dyspnea (especially in lifts), with some physical symptoms that may reflect anxiety and recent life stress.
- Relapsed Hypothyroidism: Medium likelihood. History of hypothyroidism, cessation of thyroxine, timing of symptoms fit, but some symptoms (weight loss, palpitations) are atypical for hypothyroidism.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: No direct documentation of sleep pattern, risk assessment (suicidality/self-harm), family psychiatric history, substance/alcohol use, mental status details (appearance/behavior, cognition), and formal consent. No confirmed review/follow-up date.
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: Hypothyroidism considered as differential, but doctor and DDx note conflict (palpitations and weight loss atypical for hypothyroidism)—conflict noted.
● Transcript quality notes: Patient demographic details (DOB, contact, address) incomplete; dialogue mostly clear but some responses and history elements incomplete/unexplored.
